source: Hiragana learning journey and Base Hiragana Learning Experiment in user Notion (October 2026)
note: State labels summarize historical reports, not re-assessed mastery. Sample values painted into concept images are decorative only.

skills.title: Sound Structure
skills.summary: Organized the mora sound patterns and reconstructed the underlying sound system.
skills.evidence: Documented shift from casual exposure to a recoverable sound framework.

skills.title: Kana Recognition
skills.summary: Recognized written kana and associated visual forms with the sound inventory.
skills.evidence: Flashcard exposure, matching and recognition testing were documented.

skills.title: Chart Reconstruction
skills.summary: Rebuilt the structured kana chart from a random assortment of tiles.
skills.evidence: Used scavenger-hunt-style matching to recover sounds, shapes, and positions.

skills.title: Unaided Recall
skills.summary: Retrieved kana from memory and flagged wrong or uncertain answers.
skills.evidence: Repeated recall checks and handwritten notes of slow or missed forms.

skills.title: Written Production
skills.summary: Reproduced all 46 base hiragana from memory on the documented next-day test.
skills.evidence: Delayed written production: 46/46, following an earlier roughly 89% trial.

skills.title: Authentic Reading
skills.summary: Apply kana recognition and word recall to authentic passages from Musashi.
skills.evidence: The reading and interpretation path is active/emerging, not yet certified.
